body:
Jhunjhunwala qualified as a chartered accountant and **started with ₹5,000 in 1985**. His father refused to fund him ([ThePrint](https://theprint.in/theprint-profile/rakesh-jhunjhunwala-was-investor-with-midas-touch-who-never-gave-up-on-indian-markets/1654819)). He then borrowed from his brother's clients, promising them more than fixed-deposit returns ([ThePrint](https://theprint.in/india/indias-warren-buffett-the-man-with-the-midas-touch-who-was-rakesh-jhunjhunwala/1082239)). His famous 1986 trade was **5,000 Tata Tea shares at ₹43**, which reached ₹143 in about three months ([ThePrint](https://theprint.in/theprint-profile/rakesh-jhunjhunwala-was-investor-with-midas-touch-who-never-gave-up-on-indian-markets/1654819)). That position cost about ₹2.15 lakh, more than 40 times his seed capital, so it was funded with other people's money. He said he made "my biggest wealth" in 1991–92 by being bearish during the Mehta scam ([ThePrint](https://theprint.in/india/indias-warren-buffett-the-man-with-the-midas-touch-who-was-rakesh-jhunjhunwala/1082239)). He described himself plainly: "I love trading more than investing… I never trade my investments," and "you can't make money on borrowed knowledge" ([Outlook Business](https://www.outlookbusiness.com/interview/you-cant-make-money-on-borrowed-knowledge-566)).

Titan made the legend. By his own account he bought around **₹30 in October 2001**, and he held through volatility because "there was no permanent impairment of value" ([Outlook Business](https://www.outlookbusiness.com/interview/you-cant-make-money-on-borrowed-knowledge-566)). Filings show 664,250 shares bought between March and June 2002 at around ₹50 unadjusted ([Open Magazine](https://openthemagazine.com/features/living/jhunjhunwalas-real-bull-run)). The "₹3" figure is the split- and bonus-adjusted price ([Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/top-story/story/80000-return-in-20-years-atul-suri-explains-how-mentor-rakesh-jhunjunwala-spotted-titan-stock-346458-2022-09-06)). At his death in August 2022, his 5.1% Titan stake was worth **₹11,087 crore, about a third of a 32-stock portfolio** ([ThePrint](https://theprint.in/india/indias-warren-buffett-the-man-with-the-midas-touch-who-was-rakesh-jhunjhunwala/1082239); [BNN Bloomberg](https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/indian-billionaire-s-stock-holdings-worth-nearly-4-billion-in-focus-after-death-1.1806140.amp.html)). Take Titan out and his record is still strong, but it is no longer extraordinary.

body: On 3 July 2025 SEBI barred Jane Street (JS Group) from Indian markets and impounded about ₹4,843.5 crore (~$567m) of alleged unlawful gains. SEBI alleged the group used cash and futures trades in Bank Nifty constituents to move the index in favour of much larger options positions. Over Jan 2023 to Mar 2025 the group's net profit was ₹36,502 crore, so the user's "~₹36,500 crore" is verified. The ban was lifted on about 18 July 2025 after the escrow deposit. As of Nov 2026 there is no final order. Litigation at SAT is over document disclosure, and SAT reserved its order on 21 Oct 2026. I found no ruling after that date.

body: For both men, the most verifiable income comes from fees charged to followers, not their own trading. Veliyath's reputation funds a PMS/AIF charging 2% plus 10% above a 10% hurdle. Sundar's following funded advisory calls (₹4.6 crore over about two-plus years per SEBI) and workshops. SEBI enforcement since 2023 has targeted exactly this pattern: unregistered "education" that is really advice.

body:
- **Edge before stocks.** Don't jump to producing stock lists. First ask: what is our
  advantage on this question that the market doesn't have? Public screens = no edge.
- **Ask what the user actually asked.** Don't substitute output for thinking. If the
  user hasn't asked for picks, don't hand them picks.
- **Verify every number** against two dated sources (stock-research-analyst skill).
  Mark single-sourced figures. Re-derive ratios yourself.
- **Be honest, not flattering.** The user has a big dream; serve it with the truth.
  No "certain profit" language — think in probabilities, base rates, asymmetric bets,
  and survival.
- **Research, not SEBI-registered advice** — say it once, don't preach.
- HTML/reports: light theme only (user preference); use `barak-report-design` skill.
- Use they/them for the user unless told otherwise.

`case_study:ftx-2022` | 2022-11-11 | tickers: - | confidence: verified

FTX was valued at ~$32 bn in early 2022 with backers including Sequoia, SoftBank and Temasek. On 2 Nov 2022 CoinDesk (Ian Allison) published sister firm Alameda Research's balance sheet: a large share of its ~$14.6 bn assets was FTT, the token FTX itself issued ($3.66 bn 'unlocked FTT' + $2.16 bn 'FTT collateral'). Binance said on 6 Nov it would sell its FTT; withdrawals surged; FTX halted withdrawals on 8 Nov and filed for bankruptcy on 11 Nov. Customer deposits had been lent to Alameda (shortfall widely reported ~$8 bn). Sam Bankman-Fried was convicted in Nov 2023 and sentenced to 25 years in Mar 2024. (Bankruptcy estate later recovered enough to repay customers in full on petition-date values due to asset recoveries and crypto prices -- not a vindication.) Visible flags: (1) no independent board, no CFO, no risk committee; (2) a related proprietary trading firm owned by the exchange founder; (3) self-issued token used as collateral = circular value; (4) obscure auditors for a $30 bn firm; (5) offshore domicile (Bahamas) and opaque related-party loans to executives; (6) VCs admitted minimal diligence. Lesson: circular collateral and related-party trading arms are the purest disqualifiers; custody of your assets with an unregulated counterparty is credit risk.

**Lesson:** Circular collateral = zero
**Spotted early by:** CoinDesk (Ian Allison); Binance
**Links:** illustrates -> `insight:disqualifiers`, illustrates -> `insight:avoid-ruin`
